subject.title: fix(reef): bound relay HTTP JSON response body reads

question: Should Reef formally accept 16 MiB for successful relay JSON and 64 KiB for relay error JSON as safe protocol ceilings?
rationale: The implementation and proof are strong, but repository code and discussion do not establish the maximum legitimate Reef relay payload envelope, so automation cannot safely decide whether these availability limits are compatible.

options.title: Accept the proposed ceilings
options.body: Confirm that legitimate Reef relay responses remain comfortably below 16 MiB and errors below 64 KiB, then rebase and merge the exact head.

options.title: Adjust the ceilings first
options.body: Choose limits from the relay protocol or observed production envelope and update the constants and boundary tests before merge.

options.title: Pause pending contract evidence
options.body: Hold the PR until the relay owner or protocol documentation can establish safe maximum response sizes.

recommendation.title: Accept the proposed ceilings
recommendation.body: Confirm that legitimate Reef relay responses remain comfortably below 16 MiB and errors below 64 KiB, then rebase and merge the exact head.

likelyOwner.reason: The remaining choice is a compatibility and availability acceptance decision without a clearly established Reef-specific code owner in the available evidence.
